Pie Charts

Source: vignettes/articles/r-docs/pie-charts.Rmd
pie-charts.Rmd

Basic Pie Chart 

library(plotly.core)

USPersonalExpenditure <- data.frame("Categorie"=rownames(USPersonalExpenditure), USPersonalExpenditure)
data <- USPersonalExpenditure[,c('Categorie', 'X1960')]

fig <- data |>
  go_figure() |>
  add_pie(labels = ~Categorie, values = ~X1960) |>
  update_layout(title = "United States Personal Expenditures by Categories in 1960")

fig

Styled Pie Chart 

library(plotly.core)

USPersonalExpenditure <- data.frame("Categorie" = rownames(USPersonalExpenditure), USPersonalExpenditure)
data <- USPersonalExpenditure[, c('Categorie', 'X1960')]

colors <- c('rgb(211,94,96)', 'rgb(128,133,133)', 'rgb(144,103,167)', 'rgb(171,104,87)', 'rgb(114,147,203)')

fig <- data |>
  go_figure() |>
  add_pie(
    labels = ~Categorie,
    values = ~X1960,
    textposition = "inside",
    textinfo = "label+percent",
    insidetextfont = go_font(color = "#FFFFFF"),
    hoverinfo = "text",
    text = ~paste("$", X1960, " billions"),
    marker = go_pie_marker(
      colors = colors,
      line = go_pie_marker_line(color = "#FFFFFF", width = 1)
    ),
    # The 'pull' attribute can also be used to create space between the sectors
    showlegend = FALSE
  ) |>
  update_layout(title = "United States Personal Expenditures by Categories in 1960")

fig

Subplots

In order to create pie chart subplots, you need to use the domain attribute (go_domain()). It is important to note that the x array sets the horizontal position whilst the y array sets the vertical. For example, x = c(0, 0.5), y = c(0, 0.5) would mean the bottom left position of the plot.

library(plotly.core)
library(dplyr)

diamonds <- ggplot2::diamonds

fig <- go_figure() |>
  add_pie(
    data = count(diamonds, cut),
    labels = ~cut,
    values = ~n,
    name = "Cut",
    domain = go_domain(x = c(0, 0.4), y = c(0.4, 1))
  ) |>
  add_pie(
    data = count(diamonds, color),
    labels = ~color,
    values = ~n,
    name = "Color",
    domain = go_domain(x = c(0.6, 1), y = c(0.4, 1))
  ) |>
  add_pie(
    data = count(diamonds, clarity),
    labels = ~clarity,
    values = ~n,
    name = "Clarity",
    domain = go_domain(x = c(0.25, 0.75), y = c(0, 0.6))
  ) |>
  update_layout(title = "Pie Charts with Subplots", showlegend = FALSE)

fig

Subplots Using Grid

This example uses the layout grid attribute (go_grid()) for the subplots. Reference the row and column destination using the domain attribute (go_domain()).

library(plotly.core)
library(dplyr)

diamonds <- ggplot2::diamonds

fig <- go_figure() |>
  add_pie(
    data = count(diamonds, cut),
    labels = ~cut,
    values = ~n,
    name = "Cut",
    domain = go_domain(row = 0, column = 0)
  ) |>
  add_pie(
    data = count(diamonds, color),
    labels = ~color,
    values = ~n,
    name = "Color",
    domain = go_domain(row = 0, column = 1)
  ) |>
  add_pie(
    data = count(diamonds, clarity),
    labels = ~clarity,
    values = ~n,
    name = "Clarity",
    domain = go_domain(row = 1, column = 0)
  ) |>
  add_pie(
    data = count(diamonds, cut),
    labels = ~cut,
    values = ~n,
    name = "Clarity",
    domain = go_domain(row = 1, column = 1)
  ) |>
  update_layout(
    title = "Pie Charts with Subplots",
    showlegend = FALSE,
    grid = go_grid(rows = 2, columns = 2)
  )

fig

make_subplots() with specs of type = "domain" can also place pies in a grid. See more examples of subplots here.

Controlling text orientation inside sunburst sectors

The insidetextorientation attribute controls the orientation of text inside sectors. With “auto” the texts may automatically be rotated to fit with the maximum size inside the slice. Using “horizontal” (resp. “radial”, “tangential”) forces text to be horizontal (resp. radial or tangential). Note that plotly.js may reduce the font size in order to fit the text with the requested orientation.

library(plotly.core)

labels = c('Oxygen','Hydrogen','Carbon_Dioxide','Nitrogen')
values = c(4500, 2500, 1053, 500)

fig <- go_figure() |>
  add_pie(
    labels = labels,
    values = values,
    textinfo = "label+percent",
    insidetextorientation = "radial"
  )
fig

Donut Chart 

library(plotly.core)
library(dplyr)

# Get Manufacturer
mtcars$manuf <- sapply(strsplit(rownames(mtcars), " "), "[[", 1)

df <- mtcars
df <- df %>% group_by(manuf)
df <- df %>% summarize(count = n())
fig <- df |>
  go_figure() |>
  add_pie(labels = ~manuf, values = ~count, hole = 0.6) |>
  update_layout(title = "Donut charts using Plotly", showlegend = FALSE)

fig

Reference

See go_pie() for more information and chart attribute options!
